sampling_model.design: Uniformly draw an ordered tuple of \(G_n\) pairwise-disjoint \(M\)-subsets of \(\mathcal U_n\), then independently and completely randomize exactly \(G_{1n}\) group labels to treatment.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) labeled units and every composition-indexed potential outcome are fixed; assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is shared within each realized group, with \(p_n=G_{1n}/G_n\to p\in(0,1)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The grouped-unit fraction satisfies \(N_n/n\to\rho\in[0,1]\); no birthday-scale condition on \(N_n^2/n\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no superpopulation nuisances. The latent object affecting exact variance is \(E_{\tau,1,n}\), the degree-one Johnson energy of the arm difference.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency for a fixed finite menu of admissible group sizes under shared boundedness, their Assumption 1, and \(N_n^2/n\to0\).
Theorem 3 and the Johnson-scheme discussion provide an orthogonal harmonic basis and common eigenspaces for functions on a slice.
Proposition 3.1 records the classical eigenvalues for distance graphs in the Johnson scheme, including the Kneser relation.
Theorems 3--4 establish finite-population Gaussian limits for complete randomization on fixed experimental units.
Theorem 1 makes CR2 exactly unbiased under a specified independent-cluster working covariance model.
Theorem 1 relates regression sandwich estimators to conservative Neyman variances when clusters are fixed.
The paper characterizes optimized estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and complex designs because exact variance is generally unavailable.
Theorems 1--2 show that design-unbiased estimators can fail to concentrate under arbitrary or network interference.

tldr: Randomly formed groups cease to behave as independent regression clusters when a positive fraction of eligible units is partitioned. The exact normalized Kneser operator gives an unconditional finite-sample variance identity and a schedule-uniform expansion in which only the degree-one Johnson projection of the arm difference survives at first order; neither this expansion nor the CR2 variance comparison uses predictable-QV stabilization or scaled-variance nondegeneracy. Pointwise centered Gaussian inference and CR2 coverage are separate conditional conclusions for the named class that imposes predictable quadratic-variation stabilization for the unit-permutation-then-label-permutation filtration, together with nondegeneracy; bounded schedules alone are not claimed to imply that premise. CR2 estimates the independent-group term, so at positive density it is asymptotically conservative and is ratio-consistent exactly when the projection correction is negligible, conditional on the inference premises. When the sampling fraction vanishes, studentized normality holds without \(N_n^2/n\to0\), but this trades the comparator's Assumption 1 and birthday condition for the explicit filtration-side premise. The eight-unit witness has exact variance \(1/7\) and expected CR2 \(2/7\). Finally, the all-statistic variance-impossibility theorem holds already on the additive no-interference subclass and therefore transfers to arbitrary composition interference; its special Rademacher construction verifies predictable-QV stability separately and does not establish that property for every bounded schedule.

project_justification.gap: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} defines PAME and validates clustered inference by coupling the whole disjoint group tuple to independent draws under its Assumption 1 and \(N_n^2/n\to0\). That approximation discards first-order finite-pool dependence when \(N_n/n\to\rho>0\), while the fixed-cluster CR2 literature has no mechanism for restoring it. Bounded composition schedules by themselves also do not supply predictable quadratic-variation stabilization for the exact reveal filtration.
project_justification.niche: The disjointness relation is a Kneser operator on the uniform \(M\)-slice, so exact causal variance and the CR2 comparison can be decomposed unconditionally by Johnson degree before any Gaussian approximation is invoked. Inference is then layered on transparently for the named predictable-QV-stable class rather than presented as a consequence of boundedness.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact spectrum-weighted variance, the schedule-uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) dense expansion, and the unconditional CR2 fluctuation bound; proves that only degree one survives at the \(G_n\)-scale; and, under an explicitly separate filtration-side predictable-QV premise and scaled-variance nondegeneracy, derives a centered martingale CLT and Wald coverage. It also characterizes the CR2 sharpness frontier, verifies the versioned \({\tt clubSandwich}\) consumer and the finite witness, and proves an all-statistic exact-variance impossibility theorem using a construction-specific predictable-QV calculation and deterministic diagonal selection.

related_work: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} is the closest theorem-level comparator: its Section 3 permits a fixed finite menu of group sizes, and its Theorems 1--2 obtain asymptotic normality and CR2 ratio consistency under shared boundedness, their Assumption 1, and \(N_n^2/n\to0\). The present positive theory treats the exact homogeneous \(K=1\) structural subcase. Its exact Kneser variance and CR2 expansions are unconditional under the stated fixed-size design conditions, whereas its Gaussian and coverage conclusions replace the comparator's inference conditions by scaled-variance nondegeneracy and the explicit statistic-specific predictable-QV premise. This is an assumption trade, not a pure weakening, because predictable-QV stabilization is not derived for the full bounded-schedule class. Positive homogeneous conclusions are not claimed for variable group sizes. Theorems 1 and 3 and the Johnson association-scheme discussion of \cite{Filmus2016} provide the harmonic architecture; Proposition 3.1 of \cite{BrouwerEtAl2018} supplies the classical Kneser spectrum, and the present work derives the causal covariance quadratic form. Section 2.2 and Theorems 3--4 of \cite{LiDing2017} inform complete randomization, while \cite{Pollard1984}, Theorem VIII.1, supplies the martingale-array implication after predictable variation and conditional Lindeberg have been established or imposed as stated. The versioned \({\tt clubSandwich}\) 0.7.0 and \({\tt sandwich}\) 3.1-3 source contracts supply the software assembly, default-target, adjustment, bread, and scale semantics used by the exact consumer proposition; \cite{PustejovskyTipton2018} explains CR2 calibration under independent-cluster working models, and \cite{SuDing2021} gives the fixed-cluster design-based regression comparison. None supplies the random-partition projection correction. \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} studies optimized estimable conservative quadratic bounds when exact variance is inaccessible, and \cite{BasseAiroldi2018} supplies general interference nonconcentration logic; neither subsumes the proved equal-observation dense-PAME lower bound. That lower bound holds on an additive no-interference subclass and hence transfers to the full arbitrary-composition class. \cite{AronowGreenLee2014} gives sharp variance bounds for ordinary complete randomization, whereas global composition-table completion is a distinct unselected seed. \cite{BasseDingFellerToulis2024} and \cite{PuelzBasseFellerToulis2022} obtain exact tests by making peer-effect nulls sharp through symmetry or conditioning; PAME remains non-sharp from one random partition.
technical_internal_limitation: Finite-sample CR2 conservativeness is not asserted: the exact bias is \(-C_{\tau\tau,n}\), and higher Johnson eigenvalues alternate in sign. Conservativeness emerges at the \(G_n\)-scale because only the negative degree-one eigenvalue survives. Predictable quadratic-variation stabilization is a filtration-side conditional premise for the general CLT and coverage results, not a consequence proved from bounded schedules; its verification for the Rademacher lower-bound priors is construction-specific. The Rademacher variance limits are separated only when \(\rho>0\); at \(\rho=0\) their gap vanishes. The \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2})\) CR2 fluctuation bound is only an upper bound, so \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\) is a benchmark crossover rather than a proved exact noise-order elbow. Positive results are restricted to the homogeneous fixed-size design.
honest_scope: The exact Kneser covariance, finite-sample design variance, schedule-uniform dense projection expansion, and CR2 variance expansion are unconditional design-based conclusions under group-count growth, stable treatment and sampling fractions, fixed \(M\), and bounded potential outcomes; scaled-variance nondegeneracy and predictable-QV stabilization are not used for those conclusions. The centered martingale CLT, CR2 studentized limits, Wald coverage, and sparse studentization conclusion are conditional on the separately named predictable-QV-stable class, with scaled-variance nondegeneracy where division by the asymptotic variance is required. No claim is made that bounded schedules establish predictable-QV stabilization. The sparse result drops \(N_n^2/n\to0\) but trades the comparator's Assumption 1 for that filtration-side premise. The exact software identity is tied to the stated equal-group unweighted intercept-plus-binary-treatment call and versioned package semantics. The impossibility theorem assumes \(G_n\to\infty\), \(p_n\to p\in(0,1)\), and \(N_n/n\to\rho\in(0,1]\), holds on additive no-interference schedules, and therefore transfers upward to arbitrary composition interference; its Rademacher priors satisfy predictable-QV stability by a separate construction-specific theorem. When \(\rho=0\), the projection correction and Rademacher limit gap vanish. No finite-sample CR2 conservativeness or variable-group-size extension is asserted.

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of labeled units in the finite population at row \(n\).

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: A fixed group size that does not vary with \(n\).

symbols.name: G_n
symbols.def: The number of disjoint groups formed at row \(n\).

symbols.name: G_{1n}
symbols.def: The fixed number of realized groups assigned treatment.

symbols.name: N_n
symbols.def: \(N_n=MG_n\le n\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: The limit of \(p_n\).

symbols.name: \rho
symbols.def: The limit of \(N_n/n\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: A constant uniform over units, compositions, treatment arms, and rows.

symbols.name: c_\sigma
symbols.def: A constant uniform over rows of the triangular array.

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: The fixed level used by the Wald interval.

symbols.name: \mathcal U_n
symbols.def: \(\mathcal U_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

symbols.name: \Omega_{n,M}
symbols.def: \(\Omega_{n,M}=\{A\subseteq\mathcal U_n:|A|=M\}\), equipped with the uniform law.

symbols.name: Y_{i,n}(z,A)
symbols.def: The outcome of unit \(i\) if its realized group is \(A\) and that group receives arm \(z\); the complete schedule is deterministic.

symbols.name: \mathbb E_n
symbols.def: Expectation under a uniform candidate group in \(\Omega_{n,M}\).

symbols.name: \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_n
symbols.def: The \(L^2\) inner product on the uniform \(M\)-slice.

symbols.name: \|\cdot\|_n
symbols.def: The norm induced by the uniform-slice inner product.

symbols.name: h_{z,n}^{\circ}
symbols.def: \(h_{z,n}^{\circ}=h_{z,n}-\mathbb E_n h_{z,n}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal H_{n,k}
symbols.def: The degree-\(k\) common eigenspace in the Johnson association scheme on \(\Omega_{n,M}\), for \(k=0,\ldots,M\).

symbols.name: \Pi_{n,k}
symbols.def: The orthogonal projection under \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_n\) onto \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\).

symbols.name: \mathsf K_n
symbols.def: The conditional expectation of a slice function at a uniform group disjoint from the argument.

symbols.name: \lambda_{n,k}
symbols.def: The eigenvalue of \(\mathsf K_n\) on \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\).

symbols.name: V_{z,n}
symbols.def: \(V_{z,n}=\langle h_{z,n}^{\circ},h_{z,n}^{\circ}\rangle_n\).

symbols.name: C_{ab,n}
symbols.def: \(C_{ab,n}=\operatorname{Cov}(h_{a,n}(A),h_{b,n}(C))\) when \((A,C)\) is uniform over ordered disjoint members of \(\Omega_{n,M}\), for \(a,b\in\mathcal Z\).

symbols.name: \mathbf A_n
symbols.def: \(\mathbf A_n=(A_{n1},\ldots,A_{nG_n})\) is uniform over ordered tuples of pairwise disjoint groups.

symbols.name: \mathbf Z_n
symbols.def: \(\mathbf Z_n=(Z_{n1},\ldots,Z_{nG_n})\) is uniform over vectors with \(\sum_g Z_{ng}=G_{1n}\), independently of \(\mathbf A_n\).

symbols.name: \tau_n
symbols.def: \(\tau_n=\mathbb E_n h_{1,n}-\mathbb E_n h_{0,n}\).

symbols.name: \sigma_n^2
symbols.def: \(\sigma_n^2=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}(\widehat\tau_n)\).

symbols.name: s_{z,n}^2
symbols.type: within-arm sample variance of observed group means
symbols.def: \(s_{z,n}^2=(G_{zn}-1)^{-1}\sum_{g:Z_{ng}=z}(H^{\mathrm{obs}}_{ng}-\bar H_{z,n})^2\), where \(G_{zn}=G_{1n}\) for \(z=1\), \(G_{zn}=G_{0n}\) for \(z=0\), and \(\bar H_{z,n}=G_{zn}^{-1}\sum_{g:Z_{ng}=z}H^{\mathrm{obs}}_{ng}\).

symbols.name: \mathbf U_n^{\mathrm{perm}}
symbols.def: A uniform permutation of \(\mathcal U_n\) whose first \(N_n\) entries, in consecutive blocks of size \(M\), generate \(\mathbf A_n\).

symbols.name: \mathbf L_n^{\mathrm{perm}}
symbols.def: An independent uniform permutation of \(G_{1n}\) ones and \(G_{0n}\) zeros that generates \(\mathbf Z_n\).

symbols.name: \mathcal F_{n,r}
symbols.def: For \(0\le r\le N_n\), \(\mathcal F_{n,r}\) reveals the first \(r\) entries of \(\mathbf U_n^{\mathrm{perm}}\); for \(N_n<r\le N_n+G_n\), it additionally reveals the first \(r-N_n\) entries of \(\mathbf L_n^{\mathrm{perm}}\).

symbols.name: D_{n,r}
symbols.def: \(D_{n,r}=\mathbb E[\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n\mid\mathcal F_{n,r}]-\mathbb E[\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n\mid\mathcal F_{n,r-1}]\).

symbols.name: Q_n
symbols.def: \(Q_n=\sum_{r=1}^{N_n+G_n}\mathbb E[D_{n,r}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,r-1}]\).

symbols.name: I_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{CR2}}
symbols.def: \(I_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{CR2}}=[\widehat\tau_n-z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}},\widehat\tau_n+z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}}]\).

symbols.name: \mathcal O_n
symbols.def: \(\mathcal O_n=(\mathcal U_n,\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n,\{Y_{i,n}(Z_{ng},A_{ng}):i\in A_{ng},1\le g\le G_n\})\).

symbols.name: \widehat S_n
symbols.def: An arbitrary measurable statistic of the single observed partition and treatment assignment.

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}
symbols.def: The class defined in \(\mathrm{Definition}~\ref{def:dense-schedule-class}\).

symbols.name: \mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}
symbols.def: Under independent Rademacher signs \(U_1,\ldots,U_n\), set \(Y_{i,n}(1,A)=Y_{i,n}(0,A)=U_i\) for every admissible \((i,A)\).

symbols.name: \mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}
symbols.def: Under independent Rademacher pairs \((U_i,V_i)\), set \(Y_{i,n}(1,A)=U_i\) and \(Y_{i,n}(0,A)=V_i\) for every admissible \((i,A)\).

definitions.name: two-stage dense random-group design
definitions.construction: Draw \(\mathbf A_n\) uniformly from ordered pairwise-disjoint \(G_n\)-tuples in \(\Omega_{n,M}\), then independently draw \(\mathbf Z_n\) uniformly from assignments with exactly \(G_{1n}\) treated groups.

definitions.name: potential-group arm table
definitions.construction: For every \(z\in\mathcal Z\) and \(A\in\Omega_{n,M}\), set \(h_{z,n}(A)=M^{-1}\sum_{i\in A}Y_{i,n}(z,A)\).

definitions.name: centered Johnson decomposition
definitions.construction: For every \(f\in L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\), write \(f-\mathbb E_nf=\sum_{k=1}^M\Pi_{n,k}f\) orthogonally under \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_n\).

definitions.name: normalized disjointness covariance
definitions.construction: Use \((\mathsf K_nf)(A)=\binom{n-M}{M}^{-1}\sum_{C:C\cap A=\varnothing}f(C)\) and \(C_{ab,n}=\langle h_{a,n}^{\circ},\mathsf K_nh_{b,n}^{\circ}\rangle_n\).

definitions.name: equal-group scalar CR2 statistic
definitions.construction: Compute the within-arm sample variances \(s_{z,n}^2\) with denominator \(G_{zn}-1\), then set \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}=s_{1,n}^2/G_{1n}+s_{0,n}^2/G_{0n}\).

definitions.name: unit-permutation-then-label-permutation Doob martingale
definitions.construction: Reveal \(\mathbf U_n^{\mathrm{perm}}\) through time \(N_n\), then \(\mathbf L_n^{\mathrm{perm}}\) through time \(N_n+G_n\); form \(D_{n,r}\) from conditional expectations of \(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n\) and set \(Q_n=\sum_r\mathbb E[D_{n,r}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,r-1}]\).

definitions.name: \mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}=\{(Y_{i,n},G_n,G_{1n})_{n\ge1}:G_n\to\infty,\ p_n\to p,\ N_n/n\to\rho,\ \sup_{n,i,z,A}|Y_{i,n}(z,A)|\le B,\ \liminf_nG_n\sigma_n^2\ge c_\sigma,\ Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\}\).

definitions.name: Rademacher predictable-variation handle
definitions.construction: Expose the additive schedules under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\) and \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\) through \(\mathcal F_{n,r}\); compute conditional second moments from the remaining unit signs, unfinished \(M\)-slots, and remaining treatment-label counts, control the variance of \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\) by bounded differences, and diagonalize high-probability prior rows.

statements.statement: For every \(n\ge2M\), \(\mathsf K_n\) acts on \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\) by \(\lambda_{n,k}=(-1)^k(M)_k/(n-M)_k\). Consequently, for centered \(f,g\in L^2(\Omega_{n,M})\) and a uniform ordered disjoint pair \((A,C)\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(f(A),g(C))=\sum_{k=1}^M\lambda_{n,k}\langle\Pi_{n,k}f,\Pi_{n,k}g\rangle_n\), and \(C_{\tau\tau,n}=\sum_{k=1}^M\lambda_{n,k}\|\Pi_{n,k}(h_{1,n}-h_{0,n})\|_n^2\).
statements.justification: This identity converts the global dependence from disjoint group formation into auditable harmonic energies with exact signs and finite-sample constants.
statements.gap: Filmus2016, Theorem 3 and the Johnson-scheme discussion, supplies the common eigenspaces, while BrouwerEtAl2018 supplies the classical Kneser spectrum; neither derives a causal design variance for random groups.
statements.consumer: The identity is the input for the dense PAME variance correction and every subsequent comparison with CR2.
statements.proof_tex:
Lemma~\ref{lem:classical-johnson-decomposition} supplies the orthogonal Johnson-degree decomposition of the uniform slice.  Let \(\mathsf A_n\) denote the unnormalized adjacency operator of the Kneser graph on \(\Omega_{n,M}\).  By Lemma~\ref{lem:classical-kneser-spectrum}, its eigenvalue on \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\) is
\[
 \mu_{n,k}=(-1)^k\binom{n-M-k}{M-k}.
\]
Every vertex has \(\binom{n-M}{M}\) disjoint neighbors, so Definition~\ref{def:kneser-covariance} gives \(\mathsf K_n=\binom{n-M}{M}^{-1}\mathsf A_n\).  Since \(n\ge 2M\), all factorials below are defined, and hence
\[
 \lambda_{n,k}
 =\frac{\mu_{n,k}}{\binom{n-M}{M}}
 =(-1)^k\frac{M!}{(M-k)!}\frac{(n-M-k)!}{(n-M)!}
 =(-1)^k\frac{(M)_k}{(n-M)_k}.
\]
The disjointness relation is symmetric and the slice law is uniform, so \(\mathsf K_n\) is self-adjoint under \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_n\).  If \(f\) and \(g\) are centered, Definition~\ref{def:johnson-decomposition}, orthogonality of the \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\), and the displayed eigenvalue give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(f(A),g(C))
 =\langle f,\mathsf K_ng\rangle_n
 =\sum_{k=1}^M\lambda_{n,k}
   \langle\Pi_{n,k}f,\Pi_{n,k}g\rangle_n.
\]
Apply this identity to each ordered pair \((h_{a,n}^{\circ},h_{b,n}^{\circ})\).  Self-adjointness gives \(C_{01,n}=C_{10,n}\), while linearity of \(\Pi_{n,k}\) gives
\[
 C_{11,n}+C_{00,n}-2C_{10,n}
 =\sum_{k=1}^M\lambda_{n,k}
   \|\Pi_{n,k}(h_{1,n}-h_{0,n})\|_n^2.
\]
This is the asserted formula for \(C_{\tau\tau,n}\).

statements.statement: Under the two-stage design, \(\mathbb E[\widehat\tau_n]=\tau_n\) and the exact finite-sample variance is \[\sigma_n^2=\frac{R_n}{G_n}+C_{\tau\tau,n}-\frac{C_{11,n}}{G_{1n}}-\frac{C_{00,n}}{G_{0n}}.\] Moreover, \(\mathbb E[\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}]=(V_{1,n}-C_{11,n})/G_{1n}+(V_{0,n}-C_{00,n})/G_{0n}\), so \(\mathbb E[\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}]-\sigma_n^2=-C_{\tau\tau,n}\) exactly.
statements.justification: The formula separates treatment randomization from the covariance retained by forming groups without replacement and gives an exact finite-sample bias identity for CR2.
statements.gap: FuSamiiWang2026, Section 4.1, discards the disjoint-pair covariance under birthday sparsity; its Theorems 1--2 do not state this exact variance or bias formula.
statements.consumer: Researchers can diagnose whether a familiar group-level sandwich omits first-order random-partition dependence.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(q_n=1-p_n=G_{0n}/G_n\) and \(x_{zg}=h_{z,n}^{\circ}(A_{ng})\).  Each \(A_{ng}\) is uniform on \(\Omega_{n,M}\), each \(Z_{ng}\) has mean \(p_n\), and the two randomizations are independent by Definition~\ref{def:random-partition-design}.  Therefore Definition~\ref{def:pame-estimator} yields
\[
 \mathbb E\widehat\tau_n
 =\mathbb E_nh_{1,n}-\mathbb E_nh_{0,n}=\tau_n
\]
and
\[
 \widehat\tau_n-\tau_n
 =\frac1{G_n}\sum_{g=1}^{G_n}
 \left\{\frac{Z_{ng}}{p_n}x_{1g}
 -\frac{1-Z_{ng}}{q_n}x_{0g}\right\}.
\]
The diagonal terms in the second moment of this sum equal \(R_n/G_n\).  For distinct \(g,g'\), complete randomization gives
\[
 \frac{\mathbb E(Z_{ng}Z_{ng'})}{p_n^2}
 =\frac{G_n(G_{1n}-1)}{G_{1n}(G_n-1)},\qquad
 \frac{\mathbb E((1-Z_{ng})(1-Z_{ng'}))}{q_n^2}
 =\frac{G_n(G_{0n}-1)}{G_{0n}(G_n-1)},
\]
and
\[
 \frac{\mathbb E(Z_{ng}(1-Z_{ng'}))}{p_nq_n}
 =\frac{G_n}{G_n-1}.
\]
The corresponding group pairs are uniform ordered disjoint pairs, so Definition~\ref{def:kneser-covariance} identifies their products with \(C_{ab,n}\).  Summing the \(G_n(G_n-1)\) ordered off-diagonal terms and using \(C_{01,n}=C_{10,n}\), proved in Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-kneser-identity}, gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sigma_n^2
 &=\frac{R_n}{G_n}
   +\frac{G_{1n}-1}{G_{1n}}C_{11,n}
   +\frac{G_{0n}-1}{G_{0n}}C_{00,n}-2C_{10,n}\\
 &=\frac{R_n}{G_n}+C_{\tau\tau,n}
   -\frac{C_{11,n}}{G_{1n}}-\frac{C_{00,n}}{G_{0n}}.
 \end{aligned}
\]

For the CR2 expectation, let \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) be the observed group means in arm \(z\), where \(m=G_{zn}\).  Marginally \(\operatorname{Var}(X_j)=V_{z,n}\) and, for \(j\ne\ell\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(X_j,X_\ell)=C_{zz,n}\).  Expanding the denominator-\(m-1\) sample variance gives
\[
 \mathbb E s_{z,n}^2
 =\frac1{m-1}\left\{mV_{z,n}-m\operatorname{Var}(\bar X)\right\}
 =V_{z,n}-C_{zz,n}.
\]
Division by \(G_{1n}\) and \(G_{0n}\) proves the asserted expectation formula.  Finally, \(R_n/G_n=V_{1,n}/G_{1n}+V_{0,n}/G_{0n}\); subtracting the exact variance identity therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-\sigma_n^2=-C_{\tau\tau,n}.
\]

statements.statement: For every array satisfying group-count growth, stable treatment and sampling fractions, and bounded potential outcomes, \[G_n\sigma_n^2=R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}+o(1).\] More precisely, \(G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}+\rho E_{\tau,1,n}\to0\) and \(C_{11,n}/p_n+C_{00,n}/(1-p_n)\to0\); all Johnson degrees \(k\ge2\) vanish at the \(G_n\)-scale uniformly over the bounded schedules.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(d_n=h_{1,n}-h_{0,n}\) and
\[
e_{k,n}=\|\Pi_{n,k}d_n\|_n^2,
\qquad k=1,\ldots,M.
\]
The complete potential-outcome schedule is fixed throughout; every probability, covariance, and variance without the subscript \(n\) is taken only over the two-stage assignment in Definition~\ref{def:random-partition-design}.
Assumption~\ref{ass:bounded-potential-outcomes} and the definition of \(h_{z,n}\) imply
\[
|h_{z,n}(A)|
\leq \frac{1}{M}\sum_{i\in A}|Y_{i,n}(z,A)|
\leq B.                                                     \tag{1}
\]
Consequently,
\[
V_{z,n}
=\mathbb E_n\!\left[(h_{z,n}-\mathbb E_nh_{z,n})^2\right]
\leq \mathbb E_n[h_{z,n}^2]
\leq B^2.                                                   \tag{2}
\]
By the orthogonal decomposition in Definition~\ref{def:johnson-decomposition},
\[
\sum_{k=1}^M e_{k,n}
=\operatorname{Var}_n\{d_n(A)\}
\leq \mathbb E_n[d_n(A)^2]
\leq 4B^2.                                                  \tag{3}
\]
Since \(N_n=MG_n\leq n\), fixed \(M\), and \(G_n\to\infty\) by Assumption~\ref{ass:group-count-growth}, we have \(n\to\infty\).  Thus it suffices to consider \(n\geq4M\).

Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-kneser-identity} gives, for \(1\leq k\leq M\),
\[
|\lambda_{n,k}|
=\frac{(M)_k}{(n-M)_k}
=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{M-j}{n-M-j}.
\]
When \(n\geq4M\), each numerator is at most \(M\), and each denominator is at least \(n-2M+1\geq n/2\).  Hence
\[
|\lambda_{n,k}|\leq\left(\frac{2M}{n}\right)^k.            \tag{4}
\]
For the degrees \(k\geq2\), equations (3)--(4) and \(G_n=N_n/M\leq n/M\) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left|G_n\sum_{k=2}^M\lambda_{n,k}e_{k,n}\right|
&\leq G_n\left(\frac{2M}{n}\right)^2
       \sum_{k=2}^M e_{k,n}\\
&\leq \frac{n}{M}\frac{4M^2}{n^2}\,4B^2
=\frac{16MB^2}{n}.                                         \tag{5}
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves, uniformly over all schedules obeying Assumption~\ref{ass:bounded-potential-outcomes}, that the combined contribution of all Johnson degrees at least two is \(O(n^{-1})\) after multiplication by \(G_n\).

For degree one, Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-kneser-identity} gives \(\lambda_{n,1}=-M/(n-M)\).  Combining this identity with (5) and \(e_{1,n}=E_{\tau,1,n}\) gives the sharper deterministic expansion
\[
G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}
=-\frac{MG_n}{n-M}e_{1,n}+O(n^{-1})
=-\frac{N_n}{n-M}E_{\tau,1,n}+O(n^{-1}).                   \tag{6}
\]

The same argument controls the arm-specific disjoint covariances.  Indeed, orthogonality and (2) give
\[
C_{zz,n}
=\sum_{k=1}^M\lambda_{n,k}
  \|\Pi_{n,k}h_{z,n}\|_n^2,
\qquad
\sum_{k=1}^M\|\Pi_{n,k}h_{z,n}\|_n^2=V_{z,n}\leq B^2.
\]
Because \(2M/n\leq1/2\), equation (4) implies \(|\lambda_{n,k}|\leq2M/n\) for every \(k\geq1\).  Therefore
\[
|C_{zz,n}|\leq\frac{2MB^2}{n}.                              \tag{7}
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:stable-treatment-fraction} supplies constants \(\delta>0\) and \(n_0\) such that \(p_n\geq\delta\) and \(1-p_n\geq\delta\) for \(n\geq n_0\).  Thus (7) implies
\[
\left|\frac{C_{11,n}}{p_n}+
       \frac{C_{00,n}}{1-p_n}\right|
\leq\frac{4MB^2}{\delta n}=O(n^{-1}).                      \tag{8}
\]

Multiplying the exact identity in Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-pame-variance} by \(G_n\), and using \(G_{1n}=p_nG_n\) and \(G_{0n}=(1-p_n)G_n\), gives
\[
G_n\sigma_n^2
=R_n+G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}
 -\frac{C_{11,n}}{p_n}-\frac{C_{00,n}}{1-p_n}.
\]
Substitution of (6) and (8) proves the schedule-uniform finite-density expansion
\[
G_n\sigma_n^2
=R_n-\frac{N_n}{n-M}E_{\tau,1,n}+O(n^{-1}).                \tag{9}
\]
No scaled-variance lower bound has been used.

Assumption~\ref{ass:sampling-fraction} and fixed \(M\) imply
\[
\frac{N_n}{n-M}
=\frac{N_n/n}{1-M/n}\longrightarrow\rho.                  \tag{10}
\]
Moreover, (3) gives \(0\leq E_{\tau,1,n}\leq4B^2\).  It follows from (6) and (10) that
\[
G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}+\rho E_{\tau,1,n}
=O(n^{-1})+
 \left(\rho-\frac{N_n}{n-M}\right)E_{\tau,1,n}
\longrightarrow0.                                         \tag{11}
\]
Equation (8) proves the second asserted vanishing relation, while (9)--(10) prove
\[
G_n\sigma_n^2=R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}+o(1).
\]
Together with (5), these equations prove every assertion of the theorem using only group-count growth, stable treatment and sampling fractions, fixed \(M\), and bounded potential outcomes.

For the unconditional CR2 comparison used downstream, fix \(z\in\{0,1\}\), put \(m=G_{zn}\), and let \(f\) be either \(h_{z,n}\) or \(h_{z,n}^2\).  Under Definition~\ref{def:random-partition-design}, the groups selected into arm \(z\) are an exchangeable ordered disjoint \(m\)-tuple.  If \(f^\circ=f-\mathbb E_nf\), direct expansion of the variance of their average gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left\{\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m f(A_j)\right\}
=\frac{\operatorname{Var}_n(f)}m
+\frac{m-1}{m}\langle f^\circ,\mathsf K_nf^\circ\rangle_n. \tag{12}
\]
By Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-kneser-identity}, orthogonality, and (4),
\[
\left|\langle f^\circ,\mathsf K_nf^\circ\rangle_n\right|
\leq\frac{2M}{n}\operatorname{Var}_n(f).                  \tag{13}
\]
Stable treatment fractions give \(m\asymp G_n\), so \(m\to\infty\) and \(m\geq2\) eventually; also \(G_n\leq n/M\).  Since (1) bounds both \(f=h_{z,n}\) and \(f=h_{z,n}^2\), equations (12)--(13) give a constant \(K<\infty\), independent of the schedule, such that
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left\{m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m f(A_j)\right\}
\leq\frac{K}{G_n}.                                         \tag{14}
\]
For every \(L>0\), the elementary inequality
\[
\mathbb E[X^2]\geq \frac{L^2}{G_n}
 \Pr\!\left\{|X|>\frac{L}{\sqrt{G_n}}\right\}
\]
applied to the centered empirical average and (14) proves an \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2})\) error for both its first and second moments.  Since \(m/(m-1)=1+O(G_n^{-1})\), the sample-variance identity in Definition~\ref{def:cr2-statistic} therefore gives
\[
s_{z,n}^2-V_{z,n}=O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2}).                \tag{15}
\]
Consequently,
\[
G_n\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-R_n
=O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2}),                                \tag{16}
\]
and combining (9) with (16) yields the entirely unconditional comparison
\[
G_n\bigl(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-\sigma_n^2\bigr)
=\frac{N_n}{n-M}E_{\tau,1,n}
 +O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}).                        \tag{17}
\]
Neither predictable quadratic-variation stabilization nor scaled-variance nondegeneracy is used in (12)--(17).  When \(N_n=o(n)\) and \(E_{\tau,1,n}\to e>0\), the deterministic term in (17) has order \(N_n/n\), whereas the proved stochastic remainder is bounded by order \(G_n^{-1/2}\asymp N_n^{-1/2}\).  These rates agree at \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\).  Because (15) is only an upper bound, this identifies a benchmark crossover and does not assert a matching stochastic lower bound.
statements.justification: The degree-one Johnson projection is the unique first-order memory of finite-pool competition, and the exact coefficient \(N_n/(n-M)\) yields a schedule-uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) remainder without any scaled-variance lower bound.
statements.gap: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} covers this design as the homogeneous \(K=1\) member of a broader fixed finite group-size menu and obtains inference using \(N_n^2/n\to0\) plus its Assumption 1. The Kneser calculation here is an unconditional exact-variance result; only the downstream Gaussian conclusions use the separate predictable-QV premise.
statements.consumer: The exact coefficient determines the positive-density standard-error comparison. The unconditional \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2})\) CR2 fluctuation upper bound yields \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\) as a benchmark crossover when \(E_{\tau,1,n}\to e>0\), without asserting a matching noise-order lower bound.

statements.statement: There is a constant \(K=K(B,M,p)\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\max_{1\le r\le N_n+G_n}|D_{n,r}|\le K/G_n\) almost surely. Hence \(\max_r|D_{n,r}|/\sigma_n\to0\), and for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\sigma_n^{-2}\sum_r\mathbb E[D_{n,r}^2\mathbf 1\{|D_{n,r}|>\varepsilon\sigma_n\}\mid\mathcal F_{n,r-1}]\to0\) in probability.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(T_n=\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:stable-treatment-fraction} supplies \(\eta>0\) such that \(G_{1n},G_{0n}\ge\eta G_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

First consider a unit-reveal time.  Given two possible values for the next unit, couple the two uniform conditional tails by transposing those two units and leaving all other permutation entries and the label permutation unchanged.  A transposition changes at most two completed \(M\)-blocks, including when one transposed entry lies beyond the first \(N_n\) positions.  Each changed group mean remains in \([-B,B]\) by Assumption~\ref{ass:bounded-potential-outcomes}; hence the two coupled terminal values of \(T_n\) differ by at most
\[
 2(2B)\max(G_{1n}^{-1},G_{0n}^{-1})\le \frac{4B}{\eta G_n}.
\]
The conditional expectation after revealing the next unit therefore ranges over an interval of this length.  Its difference from its conditional average at the preceding time, namely \(D_{n,r}\), has no larger absolute value.

At a label-reveal time, couple the two possible next labels by swapping the current label with a future occurrence of the opposite label.  At most two groups switch arms.  Switching one group changes the estimator by at most \(B(G_{1n}^{-1}+G_{0n}^{-1})\), so here
\[
 |D_{n,r}|\le 2B(G_{1n}^{-1}+G_{0n}^{-1})
 \le\frac{4B}{\eta G_n}.
\]
At a time when only one label is possible the increment is zero.  Thus the claimed bound holds with, for example, \(K=4B/\eta\), which depends only on \(B\) and the limiting allocation \(p\) (and hence is admissibly denoted \(K(B,M,p)\)).

Assumption~\ref{ass:scaled-variance-nondegeneracy} gives \(\sigma_n\ge\sqrt{c_\sigma/(2G_n)}\) eventually.  Therefore
\[
 \frac{\max_r|D_{n,r}|}{\sigma_n}
 \le K\sqrt{\frac{2}{c_\sigma G_n}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
For fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), the event \(|D_{n,r}|>\varepsilon\sigma_n\) is consequently empty for every \(r\) and every sufficiently large \(n\).  The displayed conditional Lindeberg sum is then identically zero, proving the last assertion.
statements.justification: A transposition affects at most two groups or two labels, so bounded potential outcomes deliver the martingale Lindeberg condition from primitives.
statements.gap: Pollard1984 supplies the general martingale-difference array CLT, but it does not derive the predictable variation or increment bounds for completed \(M\)-blocks followed by a fixed-count label permutation.
statements.consumer: This removes a separate maximal-increment assumption from the centered design-based CLT.

statements.statement: For every triangular array in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\), \[\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sigma_n}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).\] The only randomness is \((\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n)\); the composition-indexed potential outcomes are fixed, and the Lindeberg condition is derived in \(\mathrm{Lemma}~\ref{lem:reveal-increment-bound}\) rather than assumed.
statements.justification: Centered Gaussian inference survives dense global dependence when the actual reveal martingale has stable predictable variation.
statements.gap: LiDing2017, Theorem 4, handles complete treatment randomization conditional on fixed experimental units; Ohlsson1989 handles conventional two-stage sampling; neither covers composition-indexed scores generated by a positive-fraction disjoint partition.
statements.consumer: The result supplies design-based normal inference for PAME when independent-group coupling is asymptotically invalid.
statements.proof_tex:
The terminal sigma-field in Definition~\ref{def:reveal-martingale} reveals both randomizations, while \(\mathcal F_{n,0}\) is trivial.  Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-pame-variance} gives \(\mathbb E(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n)=0\); hence the Doob decomposition telescopes to
\[
 \sum_{r=1}^{N_n+G_n}D_{n,r}=\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n.
\]
Membership in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\) includes Assumption~\ref{ass:predictable-variance-stability}, namely \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\).  Lemma~\ref{lem:reveal-increment-bound} proves, from boundedness, stable arm fractions, and scaled-variance nondegeneracy, the conditional Lindeberg condition for \(D_{n,r}/\sigma_n\).  All increments are square integrable because they are bounded.  Lemma~\ref{lem:martingale-array-clt} therefore applies and yields
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sigma_n}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
The probability law here is solely the design law of \((\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n)\); the schedule \(Y_{i,n}(z,A)\) was held fixed throughout.

statements.statement: For every array in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\), \(G_n\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-R_n\xrightarrow{p}0\) and \[G_n(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-\sigma_n^2)-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}\xrightarrow{p}0.\] Therefore CR2 is asymptotically conservative, \(\liminf_n\Pr\{\tau_n\in I_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{CR2}}\}\ge1-\alpha\), and it is ratio-consistent if and only if \(\rho E_{\tau,1,n}/(R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n})\to0\). Along any subsequence on which \(r_n=(R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n})/R_n\to r\in(0,1]\), the CR2-studentized statistic converges to \(\mathcal N(0,r)\).
statements.justification: The theorem gives the exact dense projection-energy frontier between valid conservative studentization and ratio consistency.
statements.gap: FuSamiiWang2026, Theorem 2, proves CR2 ratio consistency only under \(N_n^2/n\to0\); PustejovskyTipton2018 calibrates CR2 under independent-cluster working models rather than finite-pool competition.
statements.consumer: The result tells users of equal-group cluster-robust regression exactly when the reported standard error is sharp and when it is conservative.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix an arm \(z\), put \(m=G_{zn}\), and let \(f\) be either \(h_{z,n}\) or \(h_{z,n}^2\).  The arm's \(m\) realized groups form an exchangeable ordered disjoint sample.  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\left(\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^mf(A_j)\right)
 =\frac{V_n(f)}m+\frac{m-1}{m}C_n(f,f),
\]
where \(V_n(f)=\operatorname{Var}_n(f(A))\).  The left side is nonnegative, and the spectral bound used in Theorem~\ref{thm:dense-projection-limit} gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\left(\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^mf(A_j)\right)
 \le \frac{V_n(f)}m+|C_n(f,f)|
 \le \frac{V_n(f)}m+\frac{K_MV_n(f)}n.
\]
Here \(m\asymp G_n\), \(G_n\le n/M\), and \(|h_{z,n}|\le B\), so the right side is \(O(G_n^{-1})\), also for \(f=h_{z,n}^2\).  Chebyshev's inequality thus shows that the empirical first and second moments in each arm converge in probability to their slice counterparts.  Since \(m\to\infty\), the identity
\[
 s_{z,n}^2=\frac{m}{m-1}\left\{m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^mf(A_j)^2-\left(m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^mf(A_j)\right)^2\right\}
\]
with \(f=h_{z,n}\) gives \(s_{z,n}^2-V_{z,n}\xrightarrow{p}0\).  Hence
\[
 G_n\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}
 =\frac{s_{1,n}^2}{p_n}+\frac{s_{0,n}^2}{1-p_n}
 =R_n+o_p(1).
\]
Combining this with Theorem~\ref{thm:dense-projection-limit} proves
\[
 G_n(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-\sigma_n^2)
 -\rho E_{\tau,1,n}\xrightarrow{p}0.
\]

Let \(D_n=R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}\).  The dense limit and scaled nondegeneracy imply \(D_n\ge c_\sigma/2\) eventually.  Boundedness also bounds \(R_n\) above.  It follows that
\[
 \frac{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}}{\sigma_n^2}-1
 =\frac{\rho E_{\tau,1,n}}{D_n}+o_p(1).
\]
The deterministic leading term is nonnegative and bounded.  This proves asymptotic conservativeness and proves the stated if-and-only-if criterion for ratio consistency.

For coverage, take an arbitrary subsequence.  The ratios \(r_n=D_n/R_n\) are bounded away from zero and have limit points in \((0,1]\); pass to a further subsequence on which \(r_n\to r\).  The centered CLT, the preceding variance convergence, and Slutsky's theorem give
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}}}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,r).
\]
Because \(r\le1\), continuity of the normal distribution implies
\[
 \lim\Pr\{\tau_n\in I_{n,\alpha}^{\mathrm{CR2}}\}
 =\Pr\{|\mathcal N(0,r)|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
on that further subsequence.  The subsequence principle proves the asserted global \(\liminf\) coverage, and the same calculation proves the final stated subsequential limit law.

statements.statement: If the same conditions hold with \(\rho=0\), then \[\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}}}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\] under \(N_n/n\to0\), with no condition on \(N_n^2/n\). This replaces the whole-tuple birthday condition in FuSamiiWang2026, Theorems 1--2, by the statistic-specific predictable-variation condition and includes sequences such as \(N_n=n^{3/4}\), for which \(N_n^2/n\to\infty\).
statements.justification: Scalar PAME inference needs a vanishing sampling fraction, not a vanishing whole-tuple collision probability.
statements.gap: FuSamiiWang2026 imposes the birthday-scale restriction \(N_n^2/n\to0\) because its proof couples the entire group tuple, while this theorem targets only the scalar statistic.
statements.consumer: Experiments grouping \(n^{3/4}\) of \(n\) eligible units obtain justified CR2 inference despite failure of whole-design coupling.
statements.proof_tex:
When \(\rho=0\), Theorem~\ref{thm:dense-projection-limit} gives \(G_n\sigma_n^2=R_n+o(1)\), while Theorem~\ref{thm:cr2-phase-frontier} gives \(G_n\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}=R_n+o_p(1)\).  Scaled-variance nondegeneracy makes \(R_n\) bounded away from zero eventually, so
\[
 \widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1.
\]
Combining this with Theorem~\ref{thm:centered-design-clt} and Slutsky's theorem proves the displayed standard-normal limit.  The argument used only \(N_n/n\to0\), not \(N_n^2/n\to0\).  For example, after rounding to a multiple of the fixed \(M\), \(N_n\asymp n^{3/4}\) has \(N_n/n\to0\) and \(N_n^2/n\to\infty\), so it is covered.

statements.statement: Suppose \(G_{1n}\ge 2\) and \(G_{0n}\ge 2\). Let \({\tt fit}={\tt lm}(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\sim Z)\) be unweighted, with only an intercept and numeric binary group treatment, equal group size \(M\), and clusters equal the realized groups. With the default identity target, the treatment-coordinate entry of \({\tt clubSandwich::vcovCR}({\tt fit},\ {\tt cluster}={\tt group},\ {\tt type}={\tt 'CR2'})\) equals \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}=s_{1,n}^2/G_{1n}+s_{0,n}^2/G_{0n}\) exactly.
statements.justification: Freezing the exact software call prevents a theoretical group-HC2 formula from being misapplied to a different sandwich specification.
statements.gap: FuSamiiWang2026 states the equal-group formula and an implementation call, but it does not connect that software output to the dense projection correction.
statements.consumer: The proposition identifies the exact coefficient variance returned to users of \({\tt clubSandwich}\) in the design studied here.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix one realized data set and suppress the row index \(n\).  The assertion is deterministic conditional on this realization.  By \({\rm def:random\text{-}partition\text{-}design}\), every realized group has exactly \(M\) units.  For a group \(g\) assigned arm \(z\in\{0,1\}\), let \(y_g\in\mathbb R^M\) collect its individual observed outcomes, let \(\mathbf 1_M\) be the \(M\)-vector of ones, and define
\[
 H_g:=M^{-1}\mathbf 1_M^{\mathsf T}y_g=H^{\mathrm{obs}}_{ng},
 \qquad
 x_z:=\begin{pmatrix}1\\ z\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 X_g:=\mathbf 1_Mx_z^{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Write \(G_z:=G_{zn}\), so \(G_1=G_{1n}\) and \(G_0=G_{0n}\), and let \(X\) be the matrix obtained by stacking the \(X_g\)'s.  Both treatment values occur because \(G_1,G_0\ge2\); hence the two columns of \(X\) are linearly independent, so \(X\) has rank two.  Since \(M\ge2\), in particular \(M>0\).  Direct multiplication and inversion therefore give
\[
 X^{\mathsf T}X
 =M\begin{pmatrix}G_0+G_1&G_1\\G_1&G_1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 B:=(X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1}
 =\frac1M\begin{pmatrix}
 G_0^{-1}&-G_0^{-1}\\
 -G_0^{-1}&G_0^{-1}+G_1^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{2}
\]
The determinant inverted in (2) is \(M^2G_0G_1>0\).  If \(c=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}\) selects the treatment coordinate, (2) yields
\[
 c^{\mathsf T}Bx_1=\frac1{MG_1},
 \qquad
 c^{\mathsf T}Bx_0=-\frac1{MG_0}.
 \tag{3}
\]

The cited software contract \({\rm lem:clubsandwich\text{-}cr2\text{-}software\text{-}contract}\), together with the cited \({\tt lm}\)-bread contract \({\rm lem:sandwich\text{-}lm\text{-}bread\text{-}contract}\), says that the returned matrix is
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_{\mathrm{CR2}}
 =B\sum_gX_g^{\mathsf T}A_ge_ge_g^{\mathsf T}A_g^{\mathsf T}X_gB,
 \qquad
 A_g=\left(I_M-X_gBX_g^{\mathsf T}\right)^{-1/2},
 \tag{4}
\]
provided the matrices inside the inverse square roots are positive definite.  Here \(e_g=y_g-X_g\widehat\beta\) is the ordinary-least-squares residual block.  To verify the required positivity rather than assume it, set
\[
 P_M:=M^{-1}\mathbf 1_M\mathbf 1_M^{\mathsf T}.
\]
For a group in arm \(z\), (1)--(2) give
\[
 X_gBX_g^{\mathsf T}
 =\mathbf 1_M(x_z^{\mathsf T}Bx_z)\mathbf 1_M^{\mathsf T}
 =G_z^{-1}P_M.
 \tag{5}
\]
The matrix \(P_M\) is the orthogonal projection onto the span of \(\mathbf 1_M\).  Thus \(I_M-G_z^{-1}P_M\) has eigenvalue \(1-G_z^{-1}>0\) on that span, because \(G_z\ge2\), and eigenvalue \(1\) on its orthogonal complement.  This proves the positivity required in (4).  Spectral calculus applied to (5) then gives
\[
 A_g=(I_M-P_M)+a_zP_M,
 \qquad
 a_z:=\left(1-\frac1{G_z}\right)^{-1/2}
 =\sqrt{\frac{G_z}{G_z-1}}.
 \tag{6}
\]

Using (2) in \(\widehat\beta=BX^{\mathsf T}y\), and using equal group size to replace each group total by \(MH_g\), gives
\[
 \widehat\beta
 =\begin{pmatrix}\bar H_0\\ \bar H_1-\bar H_0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \bar H_z:=G_z^{-1}\sum_{g:Z_{ng}=z}H_g.
 \tag{7}
\]
Consequently the mean residual in a group \(g\) assigned arm \(z\) is
\[
 M^{-1}\mathbf 1_M^{\mathsf T}e_g=H_g-\bar H_z=:d_g.
 \tag{8}
\]
Equations (6)--(8) imply that the component of \(e_g\) orthogonal to \(\mathbf 1_M\) contributes nothing to the cluster score and that
\[
 \mathbf 1_M^{\mathsf T}A_ge_g
 =a_z\mathbf 1_M^{\mathsf T}e_g
 =Ma_zd_g.
 \tag{9}
\]
Combining (1), (3), and (9), the treatment-coordinate adjusted score is
\[
 q_g:=c^{\mathsf T}BX_g^{\mathsf T}A_ge_g
 =\begin{cases}
 a_1d_g/G_1,&Z_{ng}=1,\\
 -a_0d_g/G_0,&Z_{ng}=0.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{10}
\]
Taking the treatment-coordinate entry of (4), substituting (10), then using (6) and \({\rm def:cr2\text{-}statistic}\), yields the equation-by-equation identity
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 c^{\mathsf T}\widehat\Sigma_{\mathrm{CR2}}c
 &=\sum_gq_g^2\\
 &=\sum_{z=0}^1\frac{a_z^2}{G_z^2}
   \sum_{g:Z_{ng}=z}(H_g-\bar H_z)^2\\
 &=\sum_{z=0}^1
   \frac{G_z}{G_z-1}\frac{(G_z-1)s_{z,n}^2}{G_z^2}\\
 &=\frac{s_{1,n}^2}{G_{1n}}+\frac{s_{0,n}^2}{G_{0n}}\\
 &=\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{11}
\]
No randomization, independence, moment, or limiting premise is used after fixing the realized data.  The restrictions \(G_{1n},G_{0n}\ge2\) are used exactly to make the CR2 adjustment in (6) finite and the sample variances in \({\rm def:cr2\text{-}statistic}\) well defined.  Equation (11) proves the claimed exact consumer identity.

statements.statement: For the balanced \(n=N_n=8\), \(M=2\), \(G_n=4\), \(G_{1n}=2\) witness, \(V_{1,n}=E_{\tau,1,n}=3/7\), \(C_{11,n}=-1/7\), \(\sigma_n^2=1/7\), and \(\mathbb E[\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}]=2/7\). Exhaustive enumeration over the \(105\) perfect matchings and the \(6\) balanced treatment allocations, totaling \(630\) design points, reproduces both moments.
statements.justification: A fully enumerable dense design fixes the sign, normalization, and magnitude of the projection correction.
statements.gap: No cited random-group inference result reports this finite dense witness or the factor-two CR2 excess.
statements.consumer: The witness is a regression test for symbolic derivations and for a design-aware \({\tt vcovCR}\) diagnostic.
statements.proof_tex:
For a pair \(A=\{j,k\}\), write \(h(A)=(a_j+a_k)/2\).  Among the \(\binom82=28\) pairs, six have value \(1\), six have value \(-1\), and sixteen have value zero.  Thus \(\mathbb E_8h=0\) and
\[
 V_{1,n}=\mathbb E_8h^2=\frac{12}{28}=\frac37.
\]
Moreover \(h(A)=2^{-1}\sum_{i\in A}a_i\) is degree one: averaging it over a disjoint pair gives
\[
 (\mathsf K_8h)(A)=\frac1{6}\sum_{i\notin A}a_i
 =-\frac1{6}\sum_{i\in A}a_i=-\frac13h(A).
\]
Thus \(E_{\tau,1,n}=\|h\|_8^2=3/7\).  Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-kneser-identity} gives \(C_{11,n}=(-1/3)(3/7)=-1/7\), while all control quantities vanish.  Since \(p_n=1/2\), Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-pame-variance} gives
\[
 \sigma_n^2=\frac{(3/7)/(1/2)}4-\frac17-\frac{-1/7}{2}=\frac17
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}
 =\frac{V_{1,n}-C_{11,n}}{G_{1n}}
 =\frac{3/7+1/7}{2}=\frac27.
\]
There are \((8-1)!!=105\) perfect matchings and \(\binom42=6\) treated-pair choices per matching.  Directly summing \(\widehat\tau_n^2\) and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}\) over these \(630\) equally likely points gives respectively \(630/7\) and \(1260/7\); division by \(630\) reproduces \(1/7\) and \(2/7\).  The estimator mean is zero by sign balance (or by Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-pame-variance}), so the first moment calculation is the variance.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\) and \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\), the induced laws of \(\mathcal O_n\) are exactly equal for every \(n\). Suppose \(G_n\to\infty\), \(p_n\to p\in(0,1)\), and \(N_n/n\to\rho\in(0,1]\). With prior probability tending to one, \(V_{1,n}\to1/M\), \(V_{0,n}\to1/M\), and \(E_{\tau,1,n}\to0\) under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\), whereas \(E_{\tau,1,n}\to2/M\) under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\). Hence \(G_n\sigma_n^2\to1/(Mp(1-p))\) under the first prior and \(G_n\sigma_n^2\to1/(Mp(1-p))-2\rho/M\) under the second. The limit gap is \(2\rho/M>0\), and the smaller limit satisfies \(1/(Mp(1-p))-2\rho/M\ge2/M\). Consequently, for every fixed \(c_\sigma\) with \(0<c_\sigma<1/(Mp(1-p))-2\rho/M\), the probability of \(G_n\sigma_n^2\ge c_\sigma\) tends to one under each prior; the separated-limit claim is therefore confined to dense rows \(\rho>0\) that satisfy scaled-variance nondegeneracy with high prior probability.
statements.justification: The equal observation mixtures isolate the unobserved degree-one cross-arm energy as the obstruction to exact variance recovery.
statements.gap: BasseAiroldi2018 gives broad nonconcentration examples and HarshawMiddletonSavje2026 explains variance nonidentification, but neither constructs equal-law priors with separated dense PAME variance limits.
statements.consumer: This is the quantitative input to a Le Cam lower bound for every one-realization variance statistic.
statements.proof_tex:
For an additive schedule write \(x_{iz}=Y_{i,n}(z,A)\), independently of \(A\), and \(\bar x_z=n^{-1}\sum_i x_{iz}\).  Then
\[
 h_{z,n}(A)-\bar x_z=\frac1M\sum_{i\in A}(x_{iz}-\bar x_z).
\]
If \(w_i=x_{iz}-\bar x_z\), then \(\sum_iw_i=0\), and direct sampling-without-replacement algebra gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|h_{z,n}^{\circ}\|_n^2
 &=\frac1{M^2}\left\{\frac Mn\sum_iw_i^2
 +\frac{M(M-1)}{n(n-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}w_iw_j\right\}\\
 &=\frac{n-M}{M(n-1)}\frac1n\sum_iw_i^2. \qquad\text{(1)}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Also, conditioning on \(A\), the mean of this centered function over a disjoint \(M\)-set is
\[
 \frac1{n-M}\sum_{i\notin A}w_i
 =-\frac M{n-M}\left(\frac1M\sum_{i\in A}w_i\right).
\]
Thus it lies in Johnson degree one.  Formula (1) consequently applies to the degree-one energy of every additive arm difference.

Under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\), the empirical variances of both arm arrays converge in prior probability to one, while the arm difference is identically zero.  Under \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\), the two empirical variances converge to one and the empirical variance of \(U_i-V_i\) converges to two.  These conclusions follow directly from Chebyshev's inequality because the relevant iid variables are bounded and have the stated expectations.  Since \((n-M)/(n-1)\to1\), (1) proves
\[
 V_{1,n},V_{0,n}\longrightarrow\frac1M,\qquad
 E_{\tau,1,n}\longrightarrow
 \begin{cases}0,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\2/M,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}},\end{cases}
\]
in prior probability.  Because all these additive functions are degree one, Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-kneser-identity} gives \(C_{\tau\tau,n}=\lambda_{n,1}E_{\tau,1,n}\) and \(C_{zz,n}=\lambda_{n,1}V_{z,n}\).  The exact variance identity therefore gives, without invoking nondegeneracy,
\[
 G_n\sigma_n^2
 =R_n+G_n\lambda_{n,1}E_{\tau,1,n}
 -\frac{\lambda_{n,1}V_{1,n}}{p_n}
 -\frac{\lambda_{n,1}V_{0,n}}{1-p_n}.
\]
Now \(\lambda_{n,1}\to0\) and \(G_n\lambda_{n,1}=-N_n/(n-M)\to-\rho\).  Substitution of the preceding prior limits proves the two asserted limits for \(G_n\sigma_n^2\).  Their difference is \(2\rho/M\), and
\[
 \frac1{Mp(1-p)}-\frac{2\rho}{M}
 \ge\frac4M-\frac2M=\frac2M,
\]
using \(p(1-p)\le1/4\) and \(\rho\le1\).  This also proves the stated high-prior-probability nondegeneracy whenever \(c_\sigma\) is strictly below the smaller limit.

It remains to compare observations.  Conditional on any realized \((\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n)\), each sampled unit is observed in exactly one arm.  Under the common prior its observation is its independent sign \(U_i\); under the independent prior it is \(U_i\) in a treated group and \(V_i\) in a control group.  In either case the entire vector of observed individual outcomes consists of independent Rademacher variables and is independent of the design.  Unit labels, groups, and treatment labels have the same design law under both priors.  Hence the induced laws of \(\mathcal O_n\) are exactly equal.

statements.statement:
Fix \(M\ge2\), \(p\in(0,1)\), \(\rho\in(0,1]\), \(B\ge1\), and design sequences satisfying the three fraction and growth assumptions.  Put
\[
 d_{\mathrm{same}}=\frac1{Mp(1-p)},\qquad
 d_{\mathrm{ind}}=\frac1{Mp(1-p)}-\frac{2\rho}{M},
\]
and suppose \(0<c_\sigma<d_{\mathrm{ind}}\).  There are high-prior-probability sets of deterministic Rademacher schedule rows whose Cartesian diagonal selections all belong to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\); after conditioning \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\) and \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\) on these sets, their induced one-realization mixture laws have total-variation distance tending to zero, while \(G_n\sigma_n^2\) converges uniformly on the respective supports to \(d_{\mathrm{same}}\) and \(d_{\mathrm{ind}}\).  Consequently there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that every measurable \(\widehat S_n(\mathcal O_n)\) obeys
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\sup_{Y\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}}
 \Pr_Y\left(\left|\frac{\widehat S_n}{\sigma_n^2}-1\right|>\varepsilon\right)
 \ge\frac12.
\]
Thus no estimator from one realization is uniformly ratio-consistent for the exact variance over the full dense class.  The deterministic support arrays, rather than a generally unavailable pair of deterministic arrays with close laws, are the valid diagonal certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(j\in\{\mathrm{same},\mathrm{ind}\}\).  Proposition~\ref{prop:rademacher-mixture-separation} and Lemma~\ref{lem:rademacher-predictable-variation} imply the following for every fixed integer \(k\): with \(\mathbb H_n^j\)-probability tending to one,
\[
 |G_n\sigma_n^2-d_j|\le k^{-1}
\]
and, for every \(1\le m\le k\),
\[
 \mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}
 \left(|Q_n/\sigma_n^2-1|>m^{-1}\mid Y\right)\le k^{-1}.
\]
The elementary diagonal lemma therefore supplies integers \(k_n\uparrow\infty\) slowly enough that the set \(\Gamma_n^j\) on which all these inequalities hold with \(k=k_n\) satisfies \(\mathbb H_n^j(\Gamma_n^j)\to1\).  Every schedule in these sets is bounded by one.  Every deterministic selection \(Y_n\in\Gamma_n^j\) has \(G_n\sigma_n^2\to d_j>c_\sigma\); and for fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), choosing \(m\) with \(m^{-1}<\varepsilon\) in the second display proves \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\).  The deterministic design sequences already satisfy growth and the two fraction limits.  Hence every Cartesian diagonal selection belongs to \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\).  This also supplies the requested deterministic-array selection without claiming that one fixed pair of deterministic arrays must itself have close observation laws.

Let \(\widetilde{\mathbb H}_n^j\) be \(\mathbb H_n^j\) conditioned on \(\Gamma_n^j\), and let \(P_n^j\) be its induced law of \(\mathcal O_n\).  Conditioning changes a prior by total variation \(\mathbb H_n^j((\Gamma_n^j)^c)=o(1)\), and passage through the design-and-observation kernel cannot increase total variation.  The two unconditioned observation mixtures are exactly equal by Proposition~\ref{prop:rademacher-mixture-separation}.  The triangle inequality consequently gives
\[
 \|P_n^{\mathrm{same}}-P_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=o(1). \qquad\text{(9)}
\]
At the same time, by construction,
\[
 \sup_{Y\in\Gamma_n^j}|G_n\sigma_n^2(Y)-d_j|\le k_n^{-1}. \qquad\text{(10)}
\]

Write \(a=d_{\mathrm{same}}\), \(b=d_{\mathrm{ind}}\), and \(\Delta=a-b=2\rho/M>0\).  Choose \(0<\varepsilon<\Delta/(4a)\), and test the two conditioned hypotheses by declaring ``same'' exactly when
\[
 G_n\widehat S_n>(a+b)/2.
\]
By (10), for all sufficiently large \(n\), relative error at most \(\varepsilon\) forces the correct declaration under either hypothesis.  Therefore the sum of the two testing-error probabilities is no larger than the sum of the two mixture probabilities of relative estimation error exceeding \(\varepsilon\).  Conversely, the elementary testing inequality
\[
 P_n^{\mathrm{same}}(\text{error})+P_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(\text{error})
 \ge1-\|P_n^{\mathrm{same}}-P_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\]
follows directly by writing the two errors for the test's decision set.  By (9), the maximum of the two mixture estimation risks is at least \(1/2-o(1)\) at every \(n\).  Each mixture is supported on rows extendible to arrays in \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{dense}}\), so each average risk, and therefore their maximum, is bounded above by the displayed supremum over that class.  Taking the lower limit proves the claimed bound and rules out uniform ratio consistency.

statements.statement: For the Kneser graph on the \(M\)-subsets of an \(n\)-set, where adjacency means disjointness and \(n\ge2M\), the unnormalized adjacency eigenvalue on \(\mathcal H_{n,k}\) is \((-1)^k\binom{n-M-k}{M-k}\), for \(0\le k\le M\).

Let \(D_{n,r}\) be a square-integrable martingale-difference triangular array adapted to \(\mathcal F_{n,r}\), let \(\sigma_n>0\), and put \(Q_n=\sum_r\mathbb E[D_{n,r}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,r-1}]\).  If \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\xrightarrow{p}1\) and, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \sigma_n^{-2}\sum_r\mathbb E\!\left[D_{n,r}^2
 \mathbf 1\{|D_{n,r}|>\varepsilon\sigma_n\}\mid\mathcal F_{n,r-1}\right]
 \xrightarrow{p}0,
\]
then \(\sigma_n^{-1}\sum_rD_{n,r}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\).

Suppose \(G_n\to\infty\), \(p_n\to p\in(0,1)\), and \(N_n/n\to\rho\in[0,1]\).  Under either \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}}\) or \(\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}\), the unit-permutation-then-label-permutation predictable variation satisfies, jointly over the prior and design,
\[
 G_nQ_n\xrightarrow{L^2}
 \begin{cases}
 [Mp(1-p)]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
 [Mp(1-p)]^{-1}-2\rho/M,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Consequently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), under either prior,
\[
 \mathbb P_{\mathbb H_n}\!\left\{
 \mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}\!\left(
 \left|Q_n/\sigma_n^2-1\right|>\varepsilon\mid Y\right)>\varepsilon
 \right\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
We compute the predictable variation for the stipulated filtration.  Put \(q_n=1-p_n\), \(d_i=x_{i1}-x_{i0}\), and, for realized block \(A_g\),
\[
 c_g=\frac{h_{1,n}(A_g)}{p_n}+\frac{h_{0,n}(A_g)}{q_n}.
\]
Averaging first over the treatment labels shows that the martingale at unit-reveal time \(N_n\) equals the simple-random-sample mean \(N_n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{N_n}d_{U_j}\), centered at \(n^{-1}\sum_id_i\).  The remaining label-randomization residual is
\[
 \frac1{G_n}\sum_{g=1}^{G_n}(Z_g-p_n)c_g. \qquad\text{(2)}
\]
Thus \(Q_n=Q_n^U+Q_n^L\), the sums of conditional variances over the two consecutive reveal phases.

Let \(\mu_{r-1}^d\) and \(v_{r-1}^d\) be the mean and the denominator-population variance of the \(n-r+1\) unit values remaining just before unit reveal \(r\).  If \(N_n<n\), direct subtraction of the two successive conditional sample means gives
\[
 D_{n,r}^U=\frac{n-N_n}{N_n(n-r)}(d_{U_r}-\mu_{r-1}^d),\qquad
 Q_n^U=\sum_{r=1}^{N_n}\frac{(n-N_n)^2}{N_n^2(n-r)^2}v_{r-1}^d. \qquad\text{(3)}
\]
If \(N_n=n\), this phase is identically zero.  Under the common prior \(d_i=0\).  Under the independent prior the permuted \(d_i\) are iid, bounded, mean zero, and variance two.  If \(\rho<1\), all remaining populations in (3) have order \(n\), and the elementary bound \(\mathbb E|v_{r-1}^d-2|\le C(n-r+1)^{-1/2}\), obtained by expanding the empirical first two moments, applies.  Moreover, with \(L_n=n-N_n\),
\[
 G_n\sum_{r=1}^{N_n}\frac{L_n^2}{N_n^2(n-r)^2}
 =\frac{L_n^2}{MN_n}\sum_{j=L_n}^{n-1}j^{-2}\longrightarrow\frac{1-\rho}{M}. \qquad\text{(4)}
\]
If \(\rho=1\) and \(L_n\ge1\), the left side of (4) is at most \((1+L_n)/(MN_n)\to0\); it is zero when \(L_n=0\).  Equations (3)--(4) therefore give
\[
 G_nQ_n^U\xrightarrow{L^1}
 \begin{cases}0,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\2(1-\rho)/M,&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.\end{cases} \qquad\text{(5)}
\]

For the label phase, let \(s\) labels have been exposed, let
\[
 \pi_{s-1}=\frac{G_{1n}-\sum_{j<s}Z_j}{G_n-s+1},\qquad
 \bar c_{s+1:G_n}=\frac1{G_n-s}\sum_{j>s}c_j.
\]
Subtracting successive conditional expectations in (2) gives, for \(s<G_n\),
\[
 D_{n,N_n+s}^L=\frac{Z_s-\pi_{s-1}}{G_n}
 (c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G_n}),
\]
and the final increment is zero.  Hence
\[
 G_nQ_n^L=\frac1{G_n}\sum_{s=1}^{G_n-1}
 \pi_{s-1}(1-\pi_{s-1})(c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G_n})^2. \qquad\text{(6)}
\]
The label process is independent of the \(c_g\)'s.  If \(L=G_n-s+1\), direct hypergeometric covariance algebra gives
\[
 \mathbb E(\pi_{s-1}-p_n)^2
 =p_nq_n\frac{G_n-L}{L(G_n-1)}.
\]
Since \(|x(1-x)-p_nq_n|\le2|x-p_n|\), averaging the square roots of these variances over \(L=2,\ldots,G_n\) shows that replacing every weight in (6) by \(p_nq_n\) changes (6) by \(o_{L^1}(1)\); boundedness of \(c_g\) is uniform because \(p_n,q_n\) are eventually bounded away from zero.

Under either prior the disjoint blocks contain independent prior signs, so \(c_1,\ldots,c_{G_n}\) are iid, bounded, and centered.  The reverse updating identity
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{G_n-1}\frac{G_n-s}{G_n-s+1}
 (c_s-\bar c_{s+1:G_n})^2
 =\sum_{g=1}^{G_n}(c_g-\bar c)^2. \qquad\text{(7)}
\]
is obtained by expanding both sides recursively.  The difference between the unweighted sum on the left of (7) and its weighted version is \(O(\log G_n)\), because \(c_g\) is uniformly bounded.  The iid law of large numbers applied to the right side therefore shows that the unweighted average in (6) converges in \(L^1\) to \(\operatorname{Var}(c_1)\).  Now
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(c_1)=
 \begin{cases}
 [Mp_n^2q_n^2]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
 M^{-1}(p_n^{-2}+q_n^{-2}),&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
 \end{cases}
\]
It follows from (6) that
\[
 G_nQ_n^L\xrightarrow{L^1}
 \begin{cases}
 [Mpq]^{-1},&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{same}},\\
 M^{-1}(q/p+p/q),&\mathbb H_n^{\mathrm{ind}}.
 \end{cases} \qquad\text{(8)}
\]
Adding (5) and (8), and using \(q/p+p/q+2=1/(pq)\), proves the two asserted constants.  Indeed, the coefficient sum in (4) is at most \(1/M\), because it contains \(N_n\) terms and each is at most \(L_n^{-2}\), and (6) is bounded by the uniform envelope for \(c_g^2\).  Thus all scaled quantities in (3) and (6) are uniformly bounded; the \(L^1\) convergence upgrades to \(L^2\).  In particular, \(\operatorname{Var}(G_nQ_n)=o(1)\), which is the requested normalized-variance check.

Proposition~\ref{prop:rademacher-mixture-separation} gives convergence in prior probability of \(G_n\sigma_n^2\) to the same strictly positive constants.  Thus \(Q_n/\sigma_n^2\to1\) jointly in prior and design probability.  If
\[
 b_n(Y)=\mathbb P_{\mathbf A_n,\mathbf Z_n}
 \left(|Q_n/\sigma_n^2-1|>\varepsilon\mid Y\right),
\]
then joint convergence says \(\mathbb E_{\mathbb H_n}b_n(Y)\to0\).  Markov's inequality gives \(\mathbb P_{\mathbb H_n}\{b_n(Y)>\varepsilon\}\to0\), proving the final assertion.

 \widetilde B
 \sum_gX_g^{\mathsf T}A_ge_ge_g^{\mathsf T}A_g^{\mathsf T}X_g
 \widetilde B,
 \qquad
 \widetilde B=\frac{{\tt sandwich::bread}({\tt fit})}{N_{\rm obs}},
 \qquad
 A_g=\left\{I-X_g(X^{\mathsf T}X)^{-1}X_g^{\mathsf T}\right\}^{-1/2},
\]
